                                       PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO ESTABLISH                          §        PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                       §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                    §                       OF TEXAS

                      SOLUNA HOLDINGS, INC. COMMENTS
                TO PROPOSAL FOR ADOPTION OF NEW 16 TAC § 25.194

        Soluna Holdings, Inc. (" Soluna") respectfully submits these additional comments to the
Public Utility Commission of Texas ("Commission") to request clarification of the Proposal for
Adoption ("PFA") in Project No. 58481 filed on September 3rd

        Soluna operates large computational load facilities, including existing loads that exceed 75
MW and are co-located behind the meter.          Soluna requests that the Commission clarify the
applicability of the proposed rule in one specific scenario-for expansions of existing large-loads
that are co-located with a generation resource, but where the expansion that is less than 75 MW.

        Specifically, the Proposal for Adoption (PFA) states that it applies as follows:

       (1)     This section applies to a large load customer that has not energized
               as of the effective date of this section and that seeks:
               (A) a new interconnection at a single site that is equal to or exceeds
                   75 megawatts (MW);
               (B)   an expanded interconnection at a single site that equals or
                     exceeds 75 MW for the first time;
               (C)   an expanded interconnection at a single site that exceeds 75
                     MW and is expanding by 75 MW or more; or
               (D) to co-locate with a generation resource.
       (2)     For a large load customer that seeks an expanded interconnection,
               this section applies to the incremental load addition.


        Soluna believes that the blanket application to any large load that will "co-locate with
a generation resource" could be read more broadly than intended. As drafted, it is not clear
when an expansion at an existing co-location site would trigger the rule requirements. The
triggers should be the same for a standalone large load additions or a co-located load. In other
words, subparts (1)(A)-(C)-which describe either exceeding 75 MW for the first time or
adding 75 MW or more of incremental demand-should also apply to proposed load that is co-
located with a generator. It should not be the case that any additional load at a co-location site
        that is already over 75 MW would be subject to the rules, when that is not true for standalone
       loads. In other words, the stated applicability to any large load that is "co-located with a
       generator" could mean that any expansion at a site with load that already exceeds 75 MW-
       even a 1 MW expansion-would be subject to these rules, which does not make sense from a
       policy or practical standpoint.

                   Soluna respectfully requests clarification, or correction if needed, to avoid future
       confusion. Specifically, Soluna suggests the following revision to § 25.194(b)(4)

                                  (D)          to co-locate with a generation resource and that otherwise
                                               meets the standards in subparagraphs (A)-(Cj.

       Soluna thanks Commission Staff for all of the hard work on this challenging rule and appreciates
       Staff' s and Commission' s attention to clarifying this important issue.


                                                                    Respectfully submitted,
